title: Wake-activated neuronal populations that regulate sleep drive.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC flags: not open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links (GEO/SRA/BioProject). Zenodo search on the DOI returned 0 records; Zenodo keyword search (sleep deprivation, median raphe, c-Fos) found nothing related; DANDI (neurophysiology archive) search returned 0 dandisets. PubMed record (PMID 42618797) has no DataBank list; first authors Joo, Diester, Bitsikas (University of Basel, Biozentrum).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the experiments comes from the abstract: whole-brain activity mapping in mice after sleep deprivation, recovery sleep and circadian controls; chemogenetic/optogenetic activation and inhibition of deprivation-responsive cells in the anterior medial preoptic area and median raphe; slice electrophysiology. No animal counts, file formats or data availability statement were visible.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset found: paper is paywalled with no PMC copy, no accessions, nothing on Zenodo or DANDI under the DOI or topic. Any Nature 'source data' spreadsheets per figure could not be checked without scraping the publisher site.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked in files (none found). Any label (e.g. sleep-deprived vs control brain, or sleep amount after manipulation) would be an experimental group assignment per mouse, not a measured outcome table ready for modelling.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not verified; whole-brain activity maps (cleared-brain light-sheet images, typically hundreds of GB) and EEG/EMG recordings were not located in any repository.

a5_enough_rows.note: Count not seen. A mouse circuit-manipulation study of this design typically has tens of animals per group, far below ~400 labelled units even for classification; the independent unit is the mouse.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Raw whole-brain imaging would exceed 5 GB; processed region-level counts would fit but were not found.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to compare: no counts in the abstract and no files.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels would be experimental conditions assigned by the researchers (deprived vs rested), so not circular, but nothing was available to trace.

integration.partner_dataset: Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas / Allen CCF (common coordinate framework) region annotations, if region-level activity counts were ever released
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do brain regions whose activity tracks sleep debt share cell types or connectivity patterns that predict which other regions also encode sleep pressure?

controls.positive_control: Not applicable (no data). The paper's own finding, preoptic area and median raphe activation after deprivation, would be the control.

honest_claim_h3: No modelling claim is possible: no data was found, and a project would at best classify a few dozen mice as sleep-deprived or rested from brain-region activity counts, among one lab's animals.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use brain-wide maps of neuron activity to predict whether a mouse has been kept awake and how much extra sleep it needs.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-mouse activity counts across brain regions after sleep deprivation, recovery sleep or normal conditions; number of mice unknown (no data found), likely tens.
plain_idea.predict: The experimental condition (deprived or rested) or the measured amount of recovery sleep from EEG (brain-wave) recordings.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would identify brain-wide activity signatures of sleep debt, but this paper already does that with statistics, and the sample is far too small for ML.

ml_idea: Classify sleep-deprived versus rested mice from whole-brain region-level activity counts; abandoned because no data was found and the animal count is almost certainly in the tens.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find the paper's data availability statement and count mice in the whole-brain mapping experiment; under ~400 kills it.

verdict_reason: A1 and A5 fail: paywalled Nature mouse circuit-neuroscience paper with no deposited dataset found (no PMC copy, accessions, Zenodo or DANDI record), and its design (behavioural manipulations in tens of mice) cannot yield the hundreds of labelled units an ML project needs.
